I think the most important thing to do is as soon as you're finished milking, put it in the freezer so it cools as fast as possible, store in the refrigerator around thirty minutes. If you do get a milk goat, it may be in your interest to lightly study what good attachment looks like, udder wise. You do not want a doe who's udders blow out, or drag the ground, due to sagging early on because of poor attachment. Also, avoid missing a milking because it can cause infection or blow out(the teat can lose structure, making it look giant and difficult to milk as well as future off spring to latch on.).

I chose lamancha because you can milk for two years without having to breed her again. If you think you might like to eat goat, I think it's a good idea to keep a different breed for that.
